name: Trollstigen
description: Eleven hairpins up a sheer valley wall past the Stigfossen waterfall, between Åndalsnes and Valldal; closed in winter

name: Geiranger and the Eagle Road
description: Down the Ørnesvingen hairpins to the Geirangerfjord and up to Dalsnibba's viewpoint at 1,500 m; the classic link to Trollstigen

name: Atlantic Ocean Road
description: A string of low bridges and causeways hopping across skerries in the open sea between Molde and Kristiansund

name: Sognefjellsvegen
description: Northern Europe's highest mountain pass, 1,434 m, between Lom and Sogndal past the Jotunheimen glaciers; open about June to October

name: Aurlandsvegen (the Snow Road)
description: Over the bare plateau from Aurland to Lærdal, past the Stegastein viewpoint high above the Aurlandsfjord; summer only

name: Stalheimskleiva
description: Thirteen hairpins between two waterfalls, among the steepest roads in northern Europe, below the Stalheim Hotel

name: Hardangervidda (Rv7)
description: Across Europe's largest mountain plateau from Eidfjord past Vøringsfossen to Geilo; can close in winter storms

name: Lofoten (E10)
description: Island to island along the Lofoten wall to Å: fishing villages on stilts, white beaches and peaks straight out of the sea

name: Helgeland Coast Road
description: The Kystriksveien up the coast from Steinkjer to Bodø with six ferries, past the Seven Sisters and across the Arctic Circle

name: Senja
description: Norway's second-largest island: jagged outer coast, the Bergsbotn and Tungeneset viewpoints and fishing villages

name: Valdresflye
description: High mountain road to Gjende on the edge of Jotunheimen, open in summer; views of the Besseggen ridge

name: Lysevegen
description: 27 hairpins dropping to Lysebotn at the head of the Lysefjord, near Kjerag; summer only

name: Rondane (Rv27)
description: Through the mountain plateau along Rondane National Park, with the park's peaks and wild reindeer country
